species.real: Edward Lear's limericks often end by simply repeating the first line with a small change, which modern limerick writers consider cheating.
species.name: Versling

dex.text: A curl of paper with a quill for a tail, found under pub tables after limerick night. It whispers the first line of something and runs off before the rude bit.
dex.fact: A limerick has five lines rhyming AABBA; Edward Lear made the form famous in his Book of Nonsense in 1846.

species.real: Limerick's Irish name is Luimneach, which is usually explained as meaning a bare or barren spot of land.
species.name: Rhymerick

dex.text: Recites at you until you give in. Every verse scans, every rhyme lands and the last line is always a little bit filthy. Insists it was born in Limerick. Nobody can prove otherwise.
dex.fact: Whether the limerick is named after the city is unproven; one theory points to an old party song with the chorus 'Will you come up to Limerick?'
